newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FCL Forests says log prices weaker.
newsitem.headline: FCL Forests says log prices weaker.

text.p: Fletcher Challenge Forests said on Wednesday that log prices were weaker at the start of the current financial year to June 1997 but that end-use customer prices were less volatile.
"An increasing focus on managing margin throughout the customer-to-resource chain will decrease our exposure to commodity log markets," FCL Forests said.
FCL Forests recently joined the consortium that bought Forestry Corp of New Zealand from the state, almost doubling its forest estate to 300,000 hectares.
"With its new critical mass, the enlarged forests operation has a strengthened market position allowing for faster access to the growing markets of Asia, China and North America," FCL Forests said.
FCL Forests earlier announced a net profit of NZ$74 million for the year to June, up nine percent on the previous year.
A surplus provison of NZ$10 million relating to the settlement of the log price arbitration with Forestry Corp was released to income during the year.

Net earnings were also influenced by a seven percent increase in volume of logs sold over the previous year, an improvement in the grade mix of harvested log prices in the second half of the year and the appreciation of the New Zealand dollar.
Operating cashflow of NZ$129 million was seven percent lower than in the 1995 financial year.
